strings.name: Charles H. Bennett
strings.summary: Bennett moved from chemistry and molecular dynamics to the physical foundations of information, working for decades at IBM. He analyzed reversible computation, developed BB84 quantum key distribution with Brassard, and proposed quantum teleportation with several collaborators, linking thermodynamics, cryptography and quantum theory. In 2026 he and Brassard were named recipients of the 2025 Turing Award. These results do not imply teleporting matter or faster-than-light communication.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 13, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Advanced quantum information, quantum cryptography and quantum teleportation research, laying foundations for new forms of secure communication and computing.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f1.value: New York City, United States; born in 1943.
strings.highlights.h1.title: BB84 protocol
strings.highlights.h1.text: With Gilles Brassard, proposed quantum key distribution using quantum measurement properties to detect eavesdropping.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Chemistry degree, Brandeis (1964); PhD in chemical physics, Harvard (1971).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Quantum teleportation
strings.highlights.h2.text: With five collaborators, proposed transferring an unknown quantum state using entanglement and classical communication.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Turing Award announced
strings.timeline.t1.text: Shared the 2025 Turing Award with Brassard for foundational work in quantum information science.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Teleportation paper
strings.timeline.t2.text: Six authors presented a quantum-state transfer scheme in Physical Review Letters; classical communication is still required.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Quantum cryptography demonstration
strings.timeline.t3.text: Worked with Smolin, Brassard and students on an early experimental demonstration of BB84.
strings.timeline.t4.title: BB84 proposed
strings.timeline.t4.text: Published a quantum cryptography protocol with Brassard, providing an important basis for quantum key distribution.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Reinterpreted Maxwell’s demon
strings.timeline.t5.text: Linked its inability to violate the second law of thermodynamics to the cost of erasing information.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Reversible computation paper
strings.timeline.t6.text: Analyzed logically reversible computation, showing that a fixed energy dissipation is not inherent in every computing step.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctoral training completed
strings.timeline.t7.text: Studied chemical physics and molecular dynamics at Harvard, then continued research at Argonne.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Chemistry degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completed chemistry studies at Brandeis before pursuing research at Harvard.
